//-doc: Tailscale ACL — DEFAULT-DENY production access model.
Production Companion Pis are reachable on Tailscale (registered,
addressable, can phone home for ACL/cert refresh) but NO ports are
open from any other tailnet device unless tag:maintenance has been
explicitly added to the destination Pi.
Maintenance flip procedure:
1. Open https://login.tailscale.com/admin/machines
2. Find the production Pi (e.g. pi-yibc).
3. Edit tags → add `tag:maintenance` → save. Takes effect <30s.
4. SSH / web UI / satellite mirror are now reachable from tag:admin.
5. Do the work.
6. Edit tags → remove `tag:maintenance` → save. Pi locks down.
Audit: every tag mutation is logged in Tailscale's activity feed
(https://login.tailscale.com/admin/logs/configuration).
Why tag:maintenance is gated by web UI rather than ACL push:
- Per-Pi granularity (turn on YIBC, leave Saitama locked).
- No git commit per maintenance event (lower friction).
- tagOwners restricts who can apply the tag (only admins).
- Reverting in an emergency is one click, not a git revert.
What egress is allowed from production Pis:
- Local LAN (Stream Decks, AV systems) — handled at LAN layer, not ACL.
- GitLab / GitHub for ConfigMap-driven imports (if k3s mode).
- Tailscale control plane (always — required for the Pi to stay registered).
- No outbound to other tailnet members unless explicitly granted.
Tag taxonomy (multiple tags per device, NOT composite):
tag:companion        — runs Companion brain (full install)
tag:satellite        — runs Companion Satellite (Stream Deck mirror)
tag:k8s-control      — K3s server (apiserver host) — post-cutover only
tag:k8s-worker       — K3s agent / cluster member — post-cutover only
tag:env-prod         — production tier; default-deny inbound
tag:env-dev          — development tier; admin can reach freely
tag:site-yibc        — physically at YIBC
tag:site-saitama     — physically at Saitama
tag:site-home        — Jackson's home (US today, Japan future)
tag:admin            — Jackson's laptops + Mac (operator)
tag:onsite-helper    — local-engineer machines at the church (optional)
tag:maintenance      — temporary on-switch; default-deny rules bypass
A YIBC production Pi gets: tag:companion + tag:env-prod + tag:site-yibc.
A Saitama Pi gets: tag:companion + tag:env-prod + tag:site-saitama.
Jackson's Mac gets: tag:satellite + tag:env-dev + tag:site-home + tag:admin.
Jackson's laptop gets: tag:env-dev + tag:site-home + tag:admin.
When K3s cutover happens, the Pi adds: tag:k8s-control + tag:k8s-worker.
Existing tag:companion + tag:env-prod + tag:site-* stay.
Legacy tags (pre-Companion-prod work):
tag:central, tag:edge, tag:operator — kept for K3s + Karmada bootstrap
compatibility. Eventually fold into the new taxonomy.

grants.//-rule: ADMIN — outside of production. Members + tag:admin reach everything tag:env-dev or tag:site-home.
MAINTENANCE GATE — when tag:maintenance is on a Pi, tag:admin reaches it on operational ports only. Removing the tag closes the window.
SATELLITE — your home Mac (tag:satellite) connects to Companion brains during a maintenance window only. tag:maintenance must be on the Companion Pi for satellite to reach it.
ON-SITE HELPER — local engineer laptops at a church can reach their site's Pi on Companion web UI port only, only during maintenance.
K3S CONTROL PLANE — K3s servers talk among themselves for cluster ops. Always allowed. Workers reach control on apiserver port.
K3S WORKER → CONTROL — agents always need apiserver.
LEGACY central/edge — kept for K3s + Karmada bootstrap. Will fold into k8s-control / k8s-worker over time.

LEGACY admin reach to existing infra. Members + tag:admin reach tag:central + tag:edge devices (existing pi-central + pi-edge-1 from bootstrap.sh). Keeps GitLab + Karmada apiserver + Flux UI reachable while new tag taxonomy is rolled out. Will retire when those Pis are re-tagged with the new env-prod / site-* / k8s-control taxonomy.

ssh.//-rule: Self-SSH check — owner can shell into their own machines via Tailscale SSH.
Admin → maintenance window only. Tag:admin can SSH a Pi only when tag:maintenance is on the Pi.
Legacy central/edge SSH — bootstrap-time access. Phase out after K3s cutover proves stable.

tests.//-test: Default-deny: admin CANNOT reach a production Pi without maintenance tag.
Maintenance window: admin CAN reach a Pi tagged with both env-prod AND maintenance.
Satellite cannot reach Companion outside maintenance.
Onsite helper cannot reach SSH or K3s API even with maintenance.
Onsite helper reaches Companion UI during maintenance.
Legacy edge → central still works for ongoing bootstrap.
